description: Churros with Chocolate Sauce are a beloved Mexican dessert, featuring crispy fried dough sticks coated in cinnamon sugar, perfect for dipping. These golden treats offer a delightful crunch, giving way to a soft interior, making them an irresistible sweet. Paired with a rich, velvety chocolate sauce, this classic combination creates a truly decadent and satisfying experience.

instructions.title: Prepare the Churro Dough Base
instructions.text: Combine water, 2 tablespoons sugar, salt, and butter in a medium saucepan. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil over medium-high heat, stirring until the butter is melted and sugar is dissolved.

instructions.title: Add Flour and Cook Dough
instructions.text: Remove the saucepan from heat. Quickly add all the sifted all-purpose flour at once. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms a ball and pulls away from the sides of the pan. Return to low heat and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly to dry out the dough slightly.

instructions.title: Incorporate Eggs
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a large mixing bowl. Let it cool for about 5 minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition until fully incorporated and the dough is smooth and glossy. This can be done with a stand mixer or a strong wooden spoon.

instructions.title: Heat Oil and Prepare Coating
instructions.text: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or deep fryer, heat the vegetable oil to 350-375°F (175-190°C). While the oil heats, combine 1/2 cup granulated sugar and ground cinnamon in a shallow dish for the churro coating.

instructions.title: Pipe and Fry Churros
instructions.text: Spoon the dough into a large piping bag fitted with a large star tip (like an Ateco 826 or 827). Carefully pipe 4-6 inch strips of dough directly into the hot oil, using kitchen shears or a knife to cut the dough. Fry 3-4 churros at a time for 2-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crispy.

instructions.title: Coat Churros and Make Chocolate Sauce
instructions.text: Remove fried churros with a slotted spoon and drain excess oil on paper towels. Immediately toss them in the cinnamon sugar mixture until evenly coated. For the chocolate sauce, heat heavy cream in a small saucepan until simmering. Remove from heat, add chopped dark chocolate, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt. Let it sit for 2 minutes, then whisk until smooth and glossy.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.text: Arrange the warm, cinnamon-sugar coated churros on a platter alongside the rich, warm chocolate dipping sauce. Serve immediately and enjoy!

tips: For truly authentic churros, ensure your oil is at the correct temperature (350-375°F) for even cooking and a crispy texture, avoiding soggy or burnt results.
Do not skip the step of drying out the dough on the stove; this helps create a sturdier dough that is less likely to explode when fried.

Churros are best enjoyed immediately after frying and coating. If you must prepare ahead, you can fry them, cool completely, and then reheat briefly in a hot oven or air fryer before coating and serving.
article:
The irresistible crunch of a freshly fried churro, dusted with cinnamon sugar, followed by a dip into a velvety, rich chocolate sauce – it’s a culinary experience that transports you straight to the bustling streets of Mexico or a cozy café in Spain. Churros with chocolate sauce are more than just a dessert; they are a celebration of simple ingredients transformed into pure delight. This beloved Mexican dessert offers a perfect balance of crispy texture and sweet indulgence, making it a favorite across generations. If you’ve ever dreamed of recreating this magic at home, you’re in the right place. We’ll guide you through the ultimate Churros with Chocolate Sauce recipe, ensuring your homemade version rivals any you’ve tasted.

## What are Churros with Chocolate Sauce?

Churros are a fried dough pastry, typically made from choux pastry, piped through a star-tipped nozzle to give them their characteristic ridges. While often associated with Spain, where they are a popular breakfast item, churros have found a vibrant home in Mexican cuisine. In Mexico, they are a beloved street food and dessert, often enjoyed with a hot cup of coffee or a thick, spiced hot chocolate. The ridges aren't just for aesthetics; they create extra surface area, making the churro wonderfully crispy on the outside while remaining tender on the inside. The traditional pairing, and arguably the most delicious, is with a rich, warm chocolate dipping sauce. This sauce can range from a simple melted chocolate to a more complex concoction with hints of cinnamon or chili, perfectly complementing the sweet, crisp churro.

## Ingredients for Homemade Churros

Making authentic churros at home is surprisingly straightforward, requiring only a few pantry staples. Here’s what you’ll need for the basic churro dough:

*   1 cup (240ml) water
*   1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon granulated sugar
*   1/4 teaspoon salt
*   1 cup (120g) all-purpose flour
*   2 large eggs
*   Vegetable oil, for frying (about 4-6 cups, depending on your pot size)
*   For coating: 1/2 cup granulated sugar mixed with 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon

## Ingredients for the Decadent Chocolate Sauce

No Churros with Chocolate Sauce recipe is complete without a truly decadent dipping sauce. This recipe aims for a rich, slightly thick sauce that clings beautifully to the churros.

*   1 cup (170g) good quality dark chocolate chips or finely chopped dark chocolate (60-70% cacao)
*   1/2 cup (120ml) heavy cream
*   2 tablespoons granulated sugar (adjust to taste, depending on chocolate sweetness)
*   1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
*   Pinch of salt
*   Optional: 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon or a tiny pinch of cayenne pepper for a Mexican twist

## Step-by-Step Instructions: Making Churros

Get ready to transform simple ingredients into golden, crispy perfection. This Churros with Chocolate Sauce recipe starts with the dough:

1.  **Prepare the Dough Base**: In a medium saucepan, combine the water, butter, 1 tablespoon sugar, and salt. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally to melt the butter.
2.  **Add Flour**: Once boiling, remove the pan from the heat. Immediately add the all-purpose flour all at once. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture comes together to form a ball and pulls away from the sides of the pan. This is your choux pastry base.
3.  **Cool Slightly**: Return the pan to low heat and cook for another 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to dry out the dough slightly. This step helps create a crispier churro. Remove from heat and let it cool for 5 minutes.
4.  **Incorporate Eggs**: Transfer the dough to a large mixing bowl (or a stand mixer with a paddle attachment). Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition until fully incorporated and the dough is smooth and glossy. It might look curdled at first, but keep mixing until it comes together.
5.  **Prepare for Frying**: Spoon the dough into a piping bag fitted with a large star nozzle (e.g., Wilton 1M or 21).
6.  **Heat Oil**: Pour vegetable oil into a deep, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, ensuring it’s at least 2-3 inches deep. Heat the oil to 350-375°F (175-190°C). Use a candy thermometer to monitor the temperature; maintaining it is key to perfect churros.
7.  **Fry the Churros**: Carefully pipe 4-6 inch long strips of dough directly into the hot oil, using kitchen shears or a knife to cut the dough from the piping bag. Don't overcrowd the pot. Fry for 2-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through.
8.  **Drain and Coat**: Remove the fried churros with a slotted spoon and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. While still warm, toss the churros in the cinnamon sugar mixture until evenly coated. Repeat with the remaining dough. This part of the Churros with Chocolate Sauce recipe is where the magic happens!

## How to Prepare the Chocolate Dipping Sauce

While your churros are frying, you can quickly whip up the luscious chocolate sauce:

1.  **Melt Chocolate**: In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (double boiler method), or in a microwave-safe bowl, combine the dark chocolate chips and heavy cream.
2.  **Stir Until Smooth**: Heat gently, stirring frequently, until the chocolate is completely melted and the mixture is smooth and glossy. If using a microwave, heat in 30-second intervals, stirring after each, until melted.
3.  **Flavor**: Remove from heat and stir in the granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and pinch of salt. If using, add the ground cinnamon or cayenne pepper. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired.
4.  **Serve Warm**: Keep the sauce warm over very low heat or in a small slow cooker if serving immediately, or gently reheat before serving. This completes the glorious Churros with Chocolate Sauce recipe!

## Pro Tips for Perfect Crispy Churros

Achieving that ideal crispy exterior and tender interior requires a few tricks:

*   **Oil Temperature is Crucial**: Too cool, and your churros will be greasy; too hot, and they'll burn outside before cooking inside. Aim for 350-375°F (175-190°C) and use a thermometer.
*   **Don't Overcrowd**: Frying too many churros at once will drop the oil temperature and lead to soggy results. Fry in batches.
*   **Star Nozzle**: The star shape isn't just for looks; it creates more surface area, resulting in extra crispiness. Don't skip it!
*   **Dry Dough**: Cooking the dough on low heat after adding flour helps to dry it out, which contributes to a crisper final product.
*   **Coat While Warm**: The cinnamon sugar adheres best when the churros are still hot from the fryer.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Churros with chocolate sauce are incredibly versatile. While perfect on their own, here are some ideas for serving:

*   **Traditional**: Serve immediately with the warm chocolate dipping sauce. A classic Mexican breakfast or late-night treat.
*   **Beverage Pairings**: Enjoy with a strong cup of coffee, a frothy mug of Mexican hot chocolate, or a warm, comforting Atole (a traditional masa-based hot drink).
*   **Add-ons**: Dust with powdered sugar, or offer other dipping sauces like dulce de leche (caramel sauce) or a fruit jam.
*   **Dessert Bar**: For parties, set up a churro bar with various toppings and sauces, allowing guests to customize their treats. The homemade Churros with Chocolate Sauce recipe is always a hit!

## Churros Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Churros with Chocolate Sauce recipe is hard to beat, there's always room for creative twists:

*   **Fillings**: Some churros are filled after frying with dulce de leche, fruit jam, or pastry cream. You'll need a special churro filler or a piping bag with a long, thin nozzle.
*   **Flavor the Dough**: Add a pinch of cinnamon or a little orange zest to the churro dough itself for an extra layer of flavor.
*   **Different Coatings**: Beyond cinnamon sugar, consider rolling them in plain granulated sugar, powdered sugar, or even a cocoa sugar mix.
*   **Baked/Air-Fried Churros**: For a lighter option, you can bake or air-fry churros. While they won't have the exact same deep-fried crispiness, they can still be delicious. Pipe them onto parchment paper or into an air fryer basket, spray lightly with oil, and bake/fry until golden.
*   **Vegan Options**: Substitute butter with a plant-based alternative and use a "flax egg" (1 tbsp ground flaxseed meal + 3 tbsp water per egg) for a vegan-friendly Churros with Chocolate Sauce recipe.

From their humble origins to their status as a beloved Mexican dessert, churros with chocolate sauce offer a symphony of textures and flavors. Armed with this comprehensive Churros with Chocolate Sauce recipe, you're now ready to bring the joy of this iconic treat into your own home. Gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare for a truly delicious experience that will delight family and friends alike. Enjoy every crispy, chocolate-dipped bite!
